sets.title: PX4 multicopter controller defaults (PX4-Autopilot v1.13.3)
sets.note: Firmware parameter defaults from the parameter definitions at tag v1.13.3 (commit 1c8ab2a0d7db2d14a6f320ebd8766b5ffaea28fa). Airframe start-up files may override them. A unit is given only where the source states one (@unit); otherwise the condition quotes how the source defines the value. Rate-loop outputs are normalised torque commands.

values.condition: Roll P gain — Roll proportional gain, i.e. desired angular speed in rad/s for error 1 rad.
Pitch P gain — Pitch proportional gain, i.e. desired angular speed in rad/s for error 1 rad.
Yaw P gain — Yaw proportional gain, i.e. desired angular speed in rad/s for error 1 rad.
Yaw weight — A fraction [0,1] deprioritizing yaw compared to roll and pitch in non-linear attitude control.
Max roll rate — Limit for roll rate in manual and auto modes (except acro).
Max pitch rate — Limit for pitch rate in manual and auto modes (except acro).
Max yaw rate
Roll rate P gain — Roll rate proportional gain, i.e. control output for angular speed error 1 rad/s.
Roll rate I gain — Roll rate integral gain. Can be set to compensate static thrust difference or gravity center offset.

Roll rate integrator limit — Roll rate integrator limit. Can be set to increase the amount of integrator available to counteract disturbances or reduced to improve settling time after large roll moment trim changes.
Roll rate D gain — Roll rate differential gain. Small values help reduce fast oscillations. If value is too big oscillations will appear again.
Roll rate feedforward — Improves tracking performance.
Global gain of the rate controller: output = MC_ROLLRATE_K * (MC_ROLLRATE_P * error + MC_ROLLRATE_I * error_integral + MC_ROLLRATE_D * error_derivative)
Pitch rate P gain — Pitch rate proportional gain, i.e. control output for angular speed error 1 rad/s.
Pitch rate I gain — Pitch rate integral gain. Can be set to compensate static thrust difference or gravity center offset.

Pitch rate integrator limit — Pitch rate integrator limit. Can be set to increase the amount of integrator available to counteract disturbances or reduced to improve settling time after large pitch moment trim changes.
Pitch rate D gain — Pitch rate differential gain. Small values help reduce fast oscillations. If value is too big oscillations will appear again.
Pitch rate feedforward — Improves tracking performance.
Global gain of the rate controller: output = MC_PITCHRATE_K * (MC_PITCHRATE_P * error + MC_PITCHRATE_I * error_integral + MC_PITCHRATE_D * error_derivative)
Yaw rate P gain — Yaw rate proportional gain, i.e. control output for angular speed error 1 rad/s.
Yaw rate I gain — Yaw rate integral gain. Can be set to compensate static thrust difference or gravity center offset.

Yaw rate integrator limit — Yaw rate integrator limit. Can be set to increase the amount of integrator available to counteract disturbances or reduced to improve settling time after large yaw moment trim changes.
Yaw rate D gain — Yaw rate differential gain. Small values help reduce fast oscillations. If value is too big oscillations will appear again.
Yaw rate feedforward — Improves tracking performance.
Global gain of the rate controller: output = MC_YAWRATE_K * (MC_YAWRATE_P * error + MC_YAWRATE_I * error_integral + MC_YAWRATE_D * error_derivative)

Max acro pitch rate — default: 2 turns per second
Max acro yaw rate — default 1.5 turns per second

Hover thrust source selector — Set false to use the fixed parameter MPC_THR_HOVER

Source unit "norm" (normalised 0–1). Maximum thrust in auto thrust control — Limit max allowed thrust

Maximum descent velocity — Descent velocity in manual modes and offboard.

sets.title: PX4 Position defaults (PX4-Autopilot v1.13.3)
sets.note: Position/velocity control and the stabilized, altitude and position manual-mode setpoint generators. Includes landing slowdown/takeoff parameters read by the manual tasks and jerk/aggregate settings for reference, without choosing which modes or ground handling to port. SYS_VEHICLE_RESP is deliberately not ported by the draft plan; its default leaves individual parameters active. Existing vertical gains and thrust limits remain in px4. Airframe files may override firmware defaults.

values.condition: Thrust curve in Manual Mode This parameter defines how the throttle stick input is mapped to commanded thrust in Manual/Stabilized flight mode. In case the default is used ('Rescale to hover thrust'), the stick input is linearly rescaled, such that a centered stick corresponds to the hover throttle (see MPC_THR_HOVER). Select 'No Rescale' to directly map the stick 1:1 to the output. This can be useful in case the hover thrust is very low and the default would lead to too much distortion (e.g. if hover thrust is set to 20%, 80% of the upper thrust range is squeezed into the upper half of the stick range). Note: In case MPC_THR_HOVER is set to 50%, the modes 0 and 1 are the same.
Source unit "norm". Horizontal thrust margin Margin that is kept for horizontal control when prioritizing vertical thrust. To avoid completely starving horizontal control with high vertical error.
Source unit "norm". Minimum manual thrust Minimum vertical thrust. It's recommended to set it > 0 to avoid free fall with zero thrust. With MC_AIRMODE set to 1, this can safely be set to 0.
Proportional gain for horizontal position error
Proportional gain for horizontal velocity error defined as correction acceleration in m/s^2 per m/s velocity error

Integral gain for horizontal velocity error defined as correction acceleration in m/s^2 per m velocity integral Non-zero value allows to eliminate steady state errors in the presence of disturbances like wind.

Differential gain for horizontal velocity error. Small values help reduce fast oscillations. If value is too big oscillations will appear again. defined as correction acceleration in m/s^2 per m/s^2 velocity derivative
Maximum horizontal velocity setpoint for manual controlled mode If velocity setpoint larger than MPC_XY_VEL_MAX is set, then the setpoint will be capped to MPC_XY_VEL_MAX
Maximum horizontal velocity Maximum horizontal velocity in AUTO mode. If higher speeds are commanded in a mission they will be capped to this velocity.
Maximum tilt angle in air Limits maximum tilt in AUTO and POSCTRL modes during flight.
Maximum tilt during landing Limits maximum tilt angle on landing.
Maximal tilt angle in manual or altitude mode
Max manual yaw rate
Manual yaw rate input filter time constant Setting this parameter to 0 disables the filter
Deadzone of sticks where position hold is enabled
Maximum horizontal velocity for which position hold is enabled (use 0 to disable check)
Maximum vertical velocity for which position hold is enabled (use 0 to disable check)
Low pass filter cut freq. for numerical velocity derivative
Source unit "m/s^2". Maximum horizontal acceleration for auto mode and for manual mode MPC_POS_MODE 1 just deceleration 3 acceleration and deceleration 4 just acceleration
Source unit "m/s^2". Acceleration for auto and for manual Note: In manual, this parameter is only used in MPC_POS_MODE 4.
Source unit "m/s^2". Maximum vertical acceleration in velocity controlled modes upward
Source unit "m/s^2". Maximum vertical acceleration in velocity controlled modes down

Maximum jerk limit Limit the maximum jerk of the vehicle (how fast the acceleration can change). A lower value leads to smoother vehicle motions, but it also limits its agility (how fast it can change directions or break). Setting this to the maximum value essentially disables the limit. Note: This is only used when MPC_POS_MODE is set to a smoothing mode 3 or 4.
Jerk limit in auto mode Limit the maximum jerk of the vehicle (how fast the acceleration can change). A lower value leads to smoother vehicle motions, but it also limits its agility.

Altitude control mode. Set to 0 to control height relative to the earth frame origin. This origin may move up and down in flight due to sensor drift. Set to 1 to control height relative to estimated distance to ground. The vehicle will move up and down with terrain height variation. Requires a distance to ground sensor. The height controller will revert to using height above origin if the distance to ground estimate becomes invalid as indicated by the local_position.distance_bottom_valid message being false. Set to 2 to control height relative to ground (requires a distance sensor) when stationary and relative to earth frame origin when moving horizontally. The speed threshold is controlled by the MPC_HOLD_MAX_XY parameter.

Manual position control stick exponential curve sensitivity The higher the value the less sensitivity the stick has around zero while still reaching the maximum value with full stick deflection. 0 Purely linear input curve (default) 1 Purely cubic input curve

Manual control stick vertical exponential curve The higher the value the less sensitivity the stick has around zero while still reaching the maximum value with full stick deflection. 0 Purely linear input curve (default) 1 Purely cubic input curve

Manual control stick yaw rotation exponential curve The higher the value the less sensitivity the stick has around zero while still reaching the maximum value with full stick deflection. 0 Purely linear input curve (default) 1 Purely cubic input curve

Manual-Position control sub-mode The supported sub-modes are: 0 Simple position control where sticks map directly to velocity setpoints without smoothing. Useful for velocity control tuning. 3 Smooth position control with maximum acceleration and jerk limits based on jerk optimized trajectory generator (different algorithm than 1). 4 Smooth position control where sticks map to acceleration and there's a virtual brake drag

Overall Horizonal Velocity Limit If set to a value greater than zero, other parameters are automatically set (such as MPC_XY_VEL_MAX or MPC_VEL_MANUAL). If set to a negative value, the existing individual parameters are used.

Overall Vertical Velocity Limit If set to a value greater than zero, other parameters are automatically set (such as MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_UP or MPC_LAND_SPEED). If set to a negative value, the existing individual parameters are used.
Manual tilt input filter time constant Setting this parameter to 0 disables the filter

Altitude for 1. step of slow landing (descend) Below this altitude descending velocity gets limited to a value between "MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_DN" (or "MPC_Z_V_AUTO_DN") and "MPC_LAND_SPEED" Value needs to be higher than "MPC_LAND_ALT2"
Altitude for 2. step of slow landing (landing) Below this altitude descending velocity gets limited to "MPC_LAND_SPEED" Value needs to be lower than "MPC_LAND_ALT1"
Landing descend rate
Takeoff climb rate

sets.title: PX4 Allocation defaults (PX4-Autopilot v1.13.3)
sets.note: Mixer airmode selection. Enum labels are recorded in condition; no min/max is inferred from enum values. Airframe files may override firmware defaults.

values.condition: Multicopter air-mode The air-mode enables the mixer to increase the total thrust of the multirotor in order to keep attitude and rate control even at low and high throttle. This function should be disabled during tuning as it will help the controller to diverge if the closed-loop is unstable (i.e. the vehicle is not tuned yet). Enabling air-mode for yaw requires the use of an arming switch. 0 Disabled; 1 Roll/Pitch; 2 Roll/Pitch/Yaw (source @value labels).

sets.title: PX4 thrust model defaults (PX4-Autopilot v1.13.3)
sets.note: Firmware default for the static thrust-to-motor-signal model. The formula is quoted in condition, not evaluated as a derived reference value; fitting a vehicle-specific factor is later work.

values.condition: Thrust to motor control signal model parameter Parameter used to model the nonlinear relationship between motor control signal (e.g. PWM) and static thrust. The model is: rel_thrust = factor * rel_signal^2 + (1-factor) * rel_signal, where rel_thrust is the normalized thrust between 0 and 1, and rel_signal is the relative motor control signal between 0 and 1.

sets.title: PX4 hover thrust estimator defaults (PX4-Autopilot v1.13.3)
sets.note: Hover thrust estimator defaults. MPC_USE_HTE and MPC_THR_HOVER remain in px4; they are not duplicated here. Airframe files may override firmware defaults.

values.condition: Hover thrust process noise Reduce to make the hover thrust estimate more stable, increase if the real hover thrust is expected to change quickly over time.
Source unit "SD". Gate size for acceleration fusion Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.
Source unit "normalized_thrust". 1-sigma initial hover thrust uncertainty Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

Horizontal velocity threshold for sensitivity reduction Above this speed, the measurement noise is linearly increased to reduce the sensitivity of the estimator from biased measurement. Set to a low value on vehicles with large lifting surfaces.

Vertical velocity threshold for sensitivity reduction Above this speed, the measurement noise is linearly increased to reduce the sensitivity of the estimator from biased measurement. Set to a low value on vehicles affected by air drag when climbing or descending.

Source unit "normalized_thrust". Max deviation from MPC_THR_HOVER Defines the range of the hover thrust estimate around MPC_THR_HOVER. A value of 0.2 with MPC_THR_HOVER at 0.5 results in a range of [0.3, 0.7]. Set to a large value if the vehicle operates in varying physical conditions that affect the required hover thrust strongly (e.g. differently sized payloads).

sets.title: PX4 v1.13.3 takeoff, landing and land-detector parameters (Phase 6)
sets.note: Parameters read for the takeoff ramp, spool-up, automatic descent/ascent limits and the multicopter land detector. MPC_TKO_SPEED, MPC_LAND_SPEED, MPC_LAND_ALT1, MPC_LAND_ALT2, MPC_TILTMAX_LND and MPC_JERK_AUTO are already in px4Position and are not repeated. MPC_LAND_CRWL and MPC_LAND_ALT3 apply only with a range sensor. Return parameters live in returnPx4.

values.condition: Source gives no unit. Position control smooth takeoff ramp time constant. Increasing this value will make automatic and manual takeoff slower. If it's too slow the drone might scratch the ground and tip over. A time constant of 0 disables the ramp

Enforced delay between arming and takeoff. For altitude controlled modes the time from arming the motors until a takeoff is possible gets forced to be at least MPC_SPOOLUP_TIME seconds to ensure the motors and propellers can sppol up and reach idle speed before getting commanded to spin faster. This delay is particularly useful for vehicles with slow motor spin-up e.g. because of large propellers.
Automatic ascent velocity. Ascent velocity in auto modes. For manual modes and offboard, see MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_UP
Automatic descent velocity. Descent velocity in auto modes. For manual modes and offboard, see MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_DN
Max yaw rate in auto mode. Limit the rate of change of the yaw setpoint in autonomous mode to avoid large control output and mixer saturation.
Multicopter land detection trigger time. Total time it takes to go through all three land detection stages: ground contact, maybe landed, landed when all necessary conditions are constantly met.
Multicopter max climb rate. Maximum vertical velocity allowed in the landed state
Multicopter max horizontal velocity. Maximum horizontal velocity allowed in the landed state
Multicopter max rotation. Maximum allowed angular velocity around each axis allowed in the landed state.
Take-off altitude. This is the minimum altitude the system will take off to.

sets.title: Wind shear roughness length (MIL-F-8785C)
sets.note: Primary text read: MIL-F-8785C, 5 November 1980, from the EverySpec scan (the scan's text layer is poor; equations were read from page images). The unit ft is the specification's own and has no conversion in src/domain/units.ts: check isUnit before calling toSI (1 ft = 0.3048 m, exact). MIL-HDBK-1797 and 1797B were not obtained.

reference.document: MIL-F-8785C, Military Specification: Flying Qualities of Piloted Airplanes, 5 November 1980
reference.locator: 3.7.3.2 Wind shear, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 51, page image read): u_w = u20 ln(h/z0)/ln(20/z0), where z0 = 0.15 feet for Category C Flight Phase, = 2.0 feet for other Flight Phases

values.condition: Primary text (EverySpec scan of the specification, read as page images). Roughness length z0 in the mean-wind profile u_w = u20 ln(h/z0)/ln(20/z0), h and z0 in feet, u20 the wind speed 20 feet above the ground (3.7.3.1). Applies to Category C Flight Phase. The text of 3.7.3.2 states no range of h; the range 3 ft < h < 1000 ft appears only in the secondary MathWorks page. The low-altitude model of 3.7.3 is specified for all Category C operations.
